label: sec:q-gl-classical-limit-intro
html: Having stated the conjecture on the non-torsion locus, we verify that the q \to 1 degeneration recovers familiar geometry and read the resulting structure physically. The classical-limit conjecture asserts that specialising at q = 1 recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence of Beilinson–Drinfeld, and an accompanying remark sketches how the degeneration of q-opers and q-Hecke eigensheaves recovers their classical counterparts. A further remark refines this picture: the obstruction classes \kappa_n vanish identically at q = 1 but persist on the full non-torsion locus, forcing the correspondence to be intrinsically q-deformed away from the classical fibre. The section closes with two interpretive remarks, which read the equivalence as the observability condition that the fibre functor \tau supplies for a quantum observable universe.
